commenti.body:
In the same way that we have diagetic and non-diagetic music, there should be a term for when scary things are only scary because the characters are in a horror movie. 

It's something that's haunted me (pun intended) ever since I started watching horror and I wonder if anyone's written an essay about this phenomenon but I don't even know where to start.

What is the in-universe reason Patrick Bateman wore a Seiko? 

Production wise, Rolex didn’t want to be associated with the main character
You mean like someone walking down into a basement? A pretty normal thing to do, but in a horror film it can be quite scary.
Yeah exactly! Or like, going to the bathroom at night.

It's hard to ignore certain stock sound effects once you become aware of them, and they're so pervasive. Stuff like the crowd gasp, police radio scanner, children's laughter or pottery breaking. I was watching A Hidden Life and heard the squeaky iron gate sound effect. Especially noticeable in a Malick film where "naturalism" or the efforts to create the art is part of the appeal. A lot of good it is to spend half a day waiting for the perfect ray of sunshine to come through a window for one shot if you're going to then overlay it with sound effects from the 90s Sony audio library.
